draft_notes.explanation: Every blue point chooses the Chebyshev-nearest red 2x2 square, including diagonal squares. It slides adjacent only if aligned with the selected square; otherwise it stays. Exact-distance ties use a consistent reading-order convention. Direct source fits all eight D4 images of reading order to all visible demonstrations; it returns a query only when every surviving order gives the same full output. No mechanism tiers, no fallback, no query-answer access, no D4-selected tie order.
draft_notes.independent_evidence: The saved third-party atlas explanation and solver explicitly use Chebyshev nearest-square attraction, then alignment. All original fixtures fit. Canonical train[1] blue(23,13) ties between square C(rows15..16,cols10..11) and D(rows22..23,cols20..21), distance7. Visible outputs require C to win: the point stays despite alignment with D. Original query contains no contested tie. The rule is independently documented, not an invented fixture exception.
draft_notes.constructor_issue: The native sampler labels use nearest aligned square only and freeze that particular point through hidden extra_idxs=[12]. The proposed constructor preserves the old native input sampling/rejection distribution exactly, but computes returned labels from the uniform Chebyshev rule. extra_idxs becomes a compatibility parameter with no label effect. The old draw output remains an input-admissibility calculation only, never a returned training label.
draft_notes.evidence_gate: arc_agi2.nearest_square_evidence.require_nearest_square_evidence computes distance from the sets of red cells, independent of the target bounding-box distance formula. It fits all order variants to all demos and rejects unresolved query ties. Production must hold the query fixed and resample informative demonstrations. No sampling-domain narrowing.
